bottom_line: In ACE-inhibitor–intolerant heart failure patients, losartan 150 mg daily versus 50 mg daily reduced the primary composite of death or admission for heart failure (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.99).
implications: These data support that, in this studied population, losartan 150 mg daily (vs 50 mg daily) was associated with a lower hazard of the composite of death or admission for heart failure (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82–0.99), while some adverse events (eg, renal impairment, hypotension, hyperkalaemia) occurred more often at 150 mg; the trial does not provide a placebo comparison for losartan 50 mg, and it studied patients intolerant to ACE inhibitors.

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind trial comparing losartan 150 mg vs 50 mg daily in heart failure patients intolerant to ACE inhibitors.
major_points.quote: Methods This double-blind trial was undertaken in 255 sites in 30 countries. 3846 patients with heart failure ... and intolerance to angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitors were randomly assigned to losartan 150 mg (n=1927) or 50 mg daily (n=1919).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was the composite of death or admission for heart failure; analysis was intention to treat.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was death or admission for heart failure. Analysis was by intention to treat.

major_points.text: Primary composite endpoint was lower with losartan 150 mg than 50 mg.
major_points.quote: 828 (43%) patients in the 150 mg group versus 889 (46%) in the 50 mg group died or were admitted for heart failure (hazard ratio [HR] 0·90, 95% CI 0·82–0·99; p=0·027).

major_points.text: Heart-failure admission component was reduced with losartan 150 mg vs 50 mg.
major_points.quote: and 450 versus 503 patients were admitted for heart failure (0·87, 0·76–0·98; p=0·025).

major_points.text: Adverse events (renal impairment, hypotension, hyperkalaemia) were more common with 150 mg, but discontinuations were not significantly increased.
major_points.quote: Renal impairment (n=454 vs 317), hypotension (203 vs 145), and hyperkalaemia (195 vs 131) were more common in the 150 mg group than in the 50 mg group, but these adverse events did not lead to signiﬁcantly more treatment discontinuations in the 150 mg group.

major_points.text: Median follow-up was 4.7 years in each group.
major_points.quote: With 4·7-year median follow-up in each group (IQR 3·7–5·5 for losartan 150 mg; 3·4–5·5 for losartan 50 mg)

absolute_effects.text: All-cause death or heart failure admission: 828 (11.1 per 100 patient-years) vs 889 (12.4 per 100 patient-years).
absolute_effects.quote: All-cause death or heart failure admission                828                     11·1            889                                           12·4

absolute_effects.text: Heart failure admission: 450 (6.0 per 100 patient-years) vs 503 (7.0 per 100 patient-years).
Kaplan-Meier estimates at 4 years: 35.7% (150 mg) vs 38.9% (50 mg).
absolute_effects.quote: and 35·7% after 48 months in the 150 mg group, and 13·3%, 24·4%, 31·5%, and 38·9%, respectively, in the 50 mg group

absolute_effects.text: At 4 years, one additional patient without the primary event for every 31 patients treated (150 mg instead of 50 mg).
absolute_effects.quote: On the basis of Kaplan-Meier estimates at 4 years, treating patients with the 150 mg dose instead of the 50 mg dose would result in one additional patient without the primary event at 4 years for every 31 patients treated.

subgroups.text: Subgroup analyses should be interpreted with caution because no adjustment to type 1 error was made for number of subgroups examined.
subgroups.quote: Subgroup analyses should be interpreted with caution because a signiﬁcant interaction could be due to chance, since we made no adjustment to type 1 error for the number of subgroups examined.

harms.text: Hyperkalaemia (or increased potassium) occurred more often with losartan 150 mg than 50 mg.
Renal impairment (or increased creatinine) occurred more often with losartan 150 mg than 50 mg.
Hypotension occurred more often with losartan 150 mg than 50 mg.
Angioedema occurred in six patients in the 150 mg group and none in the 50 mg group.
harms.quote: Angioedema occurred in six patients in the 150 mg group and in none in the 50 mg group.

harms.text: Permanent discontinuations due to adverse events: 148 vs 133.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility criteria for patients were: age 18 years or older;
Eligibility criteria for patients were: age 18 years or older; symptomatic heart failure (New York Heart Association [NYHA] class II–IV);

exclusion_criteria.quote: Exclusion criteria were: pregnancy or lactation;
Exclusion criteria were: pregnancy or lactation; known intolerance to ARBs;

analysis_methods.text: Primary and secondary analyses were by intention to treat.
analysis_methods.quote: The analyses of the primary and secondary endpoints were by intention to treat.

analysis_methods.text: Targeted ~95% power at 4.3% significance level to detect HR 0.837; target 1710 patients with primary events.
analysis_methods.quote: To provide roughly 95% power at the 4·3% signiﬁcance level (two-sided, adjusted for interim analysis) to detect a hazard reduction of 16·3% (hazard ratio [HR] 0·837), a target of 1710 patients with primary events was set.

analysis_methods.text: Sample size increased from 3240 to 3656 in April 2004 due to lower-than-expected observed event rate.
analysis_methods.quote: On the basis of an observed overall yearly event rate of 12% (lower than was expected), the target sample size was increased from 3240 to 3656 in April, 2004.

analysis_methods.text: Formal interim efficacy analyses after about 50% and 75% of targeted 1710 adjudicated primary endpoints; O’Brien-Fleming boundary used.
analysis_methods.quote: did formal interim analyses for eﬃcacy after about 50% and 75% of the targeted 1710 adjudicated primary endpoints were detected. An O’Brien-Fleming boundary was used for interim eﬃcacy analyses.

analysis_methods.text: Time-to-event methods (Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models) used to compare dose groups for major endpoints.
analysis_methods.quote: We used time-to-event methods (Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional hazards models) to compare the 150 mg and 50 mg dose groups for major endpoints.

analysis_methods.text: Cox models included covariates for β-blocker use, region, and treatment group.
analysis_methods.quote: estimated from Cox models, with indicator variables for β-blocker use, region, and treatment group.

trial_conduct.quote: This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00090259.

trial_conduct.text: Approved by ethics committee or institutional review board of every site.
trial_conduct.quote: was approved by the ethics committee or institutional review board of every site.

trial_conduct.text: Written informed consent obtained before randomisation.
trial_conduct.quote: All patients provided their written informed consent before randomisation.

trial_conduct.text: Trial overseen by Steering Committee; safety and conduct monitored by independent DSMB; sponsor-employed statistician and DSMB members unmasked before completion.
trial_conduct.quote: The safety and conduct of the study were monitored by an independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB). A statistician (employed by the sponsor, but responsible only to the DSMB) and the DSMB members were unmasked before trial completion.

funding_declarations.quote: The sponsor of the study was involved in protocol design and undertook study and data management. All ﬁnal analyses were done by the sponsor and, independently, by a biostatistician at the University of Minnesota (JDN)

criticisms.text: Study population was limited to patients intolerant to ACE inhibitors.
criticisms.quote: Several limitations of HEAAL should be considered. We studied only patients who were intolerant to ACE inhibitors.

criticisms.text: Uncertainty whether findings would be reproduced in patients treated de novo vs those known to be intolerant of ACE inhibitors.
criticisms.quote: we cannot be certain whether our ﬁndings would be reproduced in patients being treated de novo, compared with those known to be intolerant of ACE inhibitors.

criticisms.text: Because losartan 50 mg vs placebo was not tested, magnitude of benefit for losartan 150 mg cannot be directly estimated.
criticisms.quote: Since the eﬀect of losartan 50 mg daily on outcomes related to heart failure has never been tested relative to placebo, direct estimations of the magnitude of beneﬁt of losartan 150 mg daily cannot be made

criticisms.text: Cannot establish whether greater benefit might have been achievable by combining losartan with an ACE inhibitor rather than increasing dose.
criticisms.quote: we cannot establish whether greater beneﬁt might have been achievable by combining losartan with an ACE inhibitor, rather than further increasing the losartan dose.
